newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean March notes default ratio up to 0.24 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean March notes default ratio up to 0.24 pct.

text.p: The ratio of South Korean company defaults on notes rose to 0.24 percent in March from 0.13 percent a year earlier, the central Bank of Korea said on Wednesday.
The bank said in a statement the rise was largely influenced by the defaults of Hanbo Steel Co and Sammi Steel Co, which both collapsed this year.
The default ratio was 0.24 percent in February, the bank said. The notes would include such debts as promissory notes and bank cheques.
The central bank said 1.75 trillion won worth of notes were not honoured in March out of a total 743.5 trillion won that should have been repaid.
The number of defaulting companies rose to 1,268 in March, compared with 982 a year before and 1.060 in February, the central bank said.
